36:1: Interpretation of Surah Yasin It is Meccan Abu ‘Ees al-Tirmidhi said: Qutaybah and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Rawasi narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Salih, on the authority of Harun Abu Muhammad, on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Yasin. Whoever recites Yasin, God will record for him, for reciting it, the reward of reciting the Qur’an ten times.” Then he said: This is a strange hadith, we do not know of it except through the hadith of Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, and Harun Abu Muhammad is an unknown sheikh. There is a hadith on this topic on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, but it is not authentic due to the weakness of its chain of transmission. On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him: It is under consideration. As for the hadith of Abu Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, it was narrated by Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi in his book Nawadir Al-Usul. As for the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Fadl told us, Zaid - he is Ibn Al-Habbab - told us, Hamid - he is Al-Makki, the client of the family of Al-Alqamah, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Ya Sin. Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it except Zaid on the authority of Hamid. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ishaq bin Abi Isra’il told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Ziyad, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Yasin at night will be forgiven in the morning, and whoever recites Ha-Mim, in which the smoke is mentioned, will be forgiven in the morning. Its chain of transmission is good. Ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim, a client of Thaqeef, told us, Al-Walid bin Shuja’ bin Al-Walid Al-Sakuni told us, my father told us, Ziyad bin Khaimtha told us, Muhammad bin Juhadah told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub bin Abdullah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Yasin at night seeking the pleasure of God, the Almighty, will be forgiven. Imam Ahmad said: Arim told us, Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mu'qil ibn Yasar, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Al-Baqarah is the hump and pinnacle of the Qur’an. Eighty angels descended with each verse of it, and ‘God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining’ was extracted from beneath the Throne and connected to it - or it was connected to Surat Al-Baqarah - and Yasin is the heart of the Qur’an. No man recites it, seeking God and the Hereafter, except that He forgives him. So recite it over your dead.” An-Nasa’i also narrated it in Al-Yawm wa’l-Laylah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la on the authority of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman on his authority. Then Imam Ahmad said: Arim told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman, not al-Nahdi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Recite it over your dead, meaning Surah Yasin. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i in al-Yawm wa’l-Laylah, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak with it, except that in the narration of al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar may God be pleased with him, and for this reason some scholars said: One of the characteristics of this surah is that it is not recited in a difficult matter except that God, the Most High, makes it easy, and it is as if reciting it over the dead brings down mercy and blessings, and makes the departure of the soul easier for him, and God, the Most High, knows best. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Sufyan told us: The elders used to say: If Surah Yasin is recited over the deceased, God will make his suffering easier because of it. Al-Bazzar said: Salamah bin Shabib told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I would like it to be in the heart of every person of my nation, meaning Surah Yasin. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful We have already discussed the separate letters at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that Ya Seen means O human being. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: It is also the case in the Ethiopian dialect. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: It is one of the names of God, the Most High: By the Wise Qur’an, meaning the decisive, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it. Indeed, you meaning O Muhammad, are among the messengers * On a straight path, meaning on a sound method, religion, and upright law. A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful, meaning this path, method, and religion that you have brought are a revelation from the Lord of Almighty, the Most Merciful to His believing servants, as God, the Most High, said: “And indeed, you guide to a straight path * The path of God to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to God do all matters return.” God the Almighty says: {That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are unaware}. He means by this the Arabs, for no warner had come to them before him. Mentioning them alone does not negate others, just as mentioning some individuals does not negate the generality. We have already mentioned the verses and the successive hadiths about the generality of his mission, may God bless him and grant him peace, when God the Almighty says: {Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all.}. And God the Almighty says: {The word has come into effect upon most of them}. Ibn Jarir said: The punishment has become obligatory upon most of them because God the Almighty has decreed for them in the Mother of the Book that they will not believe so they will not believe in God and they will not believe in His messengers.

36:8: The Almighty says: Indeed, We have made those who are doomed to misery, their relation to reaching guidance is like the relation of someone who has a shackle around his neck, so he gathers his hands with his neck under his chin, so his head is raised and becomes downcast. For this reason, the Almighty said: They are downcast. The one who is upcast is the one who raises his head, as Umm Zar’ said in her speech: And I drink so I am satisfied, meaning I drink and I am quenched, and I raise my head in congratulations and repose. And He was satisfied with mentioning the shackle around the neck without mentioning the hands, even though they were intended, as the poet said: I do not know if I go to a land seeking goodness, which of the two is more suitable for me? Is it the good that I seek or the evil that does not come to me? So He was content to mention good and not evil, as the speech and context indicated it. And thus, since the shackles are only known by what is combined with the hands and the neck, He was content to mention the neck instead of the hands. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him regarding the verse of God the Almighty: {Indeed, We have placed shackles on their necks, reaching to their chins, so their heads are upturned}. He said: It is like His saying the Almighty: {And do not make your hand chained to your neck}. He means by that that their hands are tied to their necks, unable to extend them for good. Mujahid said: {So they are head down}. He said: Their heads are raised, and their hands are placed over their mouths, so they are shackled from all good. And the Almighty’s saying: And We placed before them a barrier, Mujahid said: from the truth. And behind them a barrier, Mujahid said: from the truth, so they hesitate. Qatada said: in misguidance. And the Almighty’s saying: Then We covered them, meaning We covered their sight from the truth. So they do not see, meaning they do not benefit from any good, nor are they guided to it. Ibn Jarir said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that he used to recite Fa-Ghashinahum with the silent 'ayn from 'asha, which is an eye disease. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: God the Almighty made this barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. He recited: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, * Even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment. Then he said: He whom God the Almighty prevented cannot do so. Ikrimah said: Abu Jahl said: If I see Muhammad, I will do it and I will do it. Then the verse was revealed: "Indeed, We have placed around their necks shackles reaching to their chins, so their heads are upturned. * And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them so they do not see." He said: And they used to say, This is Muhammad, and he would say, Where is he, where is he? They would not see him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ziyad told me on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b who said: Abu Jahl said while they were sitting: Muhammad claims that if you follow him, you will be kings, and when you die, you will be resurrected after your death, and you will have gardens better than the gardens of Jordan, and that if you oppose him, he will slaughter you, and then you will be resurrected after your death, and you will have a fire in which you will be tormented. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to them at that time, and in his hand was a handful of dirt, and God had taken responsibility for their eyes before him, so he began to sprinkle it on their heads and recite Ya Seen * By the Wise Qur’an until he reached the verse: And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them so they do not see. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left for his needs, and they spent the night watching at his door until someone came out of the house and said: What is the matter with you? They said: We are waiting for Muhammad. He said: He has come out to you and there is not a man among you who has not placed dirt on his head, then went to relieve himself, and every man among them began to shake off the dirt from his head. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was informed of what Abu Jahl had said and he said: And I say that because they will be slaughtered by me and he is one of them. And the Most High said: And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. That is, God has sealed them with misguidance, so warning is of no benefit to them, nor are they affected by it. A similar example has already been presented at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. And as God Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment. “You can only warn those who follow the message.” That is, only the believers who follow the message, which is the Noble Qur’an, will benefit from your warning. And fears the Most Merciful unseen. That is, when no one sees him except God Almighty, knowing that God is watching him and knowing what he does. So give him good tidings of forgiveness. That is, for his sins. And a noble reward. That is, abundant, good, and beautiful. As God Almighty said: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward. Then He, the Almighty, said: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life. That is, on the Day of Resurrection. In it is an indication that God Almighty will revive the heart of whomever He wills of the disbelievers, whose hearts have died. By misguidance, then He guides them to the truth, as God Almighty said after mentioning the hardness of hearts: “Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made clear to you the signs that you may understand.” And the Almighty’s saying: And We record what they have sent forth meaning of deeds. And concerning His saying: and their traces there are two opinions: One of them We record their deeds that they themselves undertook, and their traces that they left behind, so We reward them for that also, if good then good, and if evil then evil, like the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it after him, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.” Narrated by Muslim from the narration of Shu’bah from Awn ibn Abi Juhaifa from al-Mundhir ibn Jarir from his father Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali may God be pleased with him, and in it is the story of Mujtaba al-Namar al-Mudariyyin. And it was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from his father from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ju’fi, from Abu al-Muhayyah Yahya ibn Ya’la from Abdul-Malik ibn Umair from Jarir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned the hadith in full, then… He recited this verse: And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Uwanah on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Umair on the authority of Al-Mundhir bin Jarir on the authority of his father, and he mentioned it. And likewise, another hadith in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “When the son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: beneficial knowledge, a righteous child who prays for him, or ongoing charity after his death.” Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id may God be pleased with him who said: I heard Mujahid say regarding the verse, Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind, meaning: what they left behind of misguidance. Ibn Lahi’ah narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Dinar on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr regarding the verse, And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind, meaning what they left behind. He said: whatever practice they established and then a people acted upon after their death. If it was good, then they will have a reward like theirs, without the reward of those who acted upon it being diminished in the slightest. But if it was evil, then upon them will be a burden like their sins, without the burden of those who acted upon it being diminished in the slightest. Both were mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim, and this is the preferred opinion of al-Baghawi. The second opinion is that what is meant by this are the traces of their steps towards obedience or disobedience. Ibn Abi Nujayh and others said on the authority of Mujahid, What they have put forth their deeds, and their traces he said: their steps with their feet, and this is what Al-Hasan and Qatadah said, and their traces meaning their steps. Qatadah said: If God, the Almighty, were to neglect anything about you, O son of Adam, He would have neglected what the winds erase of these traces, but He has counted all of the traces and deeds of the son of Adam until He counted this trace in what is from the obedience of God, the Almighty, or from His disobedience. So whoever among you is able to write down his trace in the obedience of God, the Almighty, let him do so. And there are hadiths with this meaning: The first hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, my father told us, al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The places around the mosque were deserted, so Banu Salamah wanted to move closer to the mosque. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said to them: I have heard that you want to move closer to the mosque. They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, we want to do that. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Banu Salamah, your dwellings record your footsteps, your dwellings record your footsteps. This is how Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sa’id al-Jariri and Kuhams ibn al-Hasan, both of them on the authority of Abu Nadrah, whose name was al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qat’ah al-Abdi, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him. The second hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti told us, Ishaq al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wanted to move closer to the mosque, so the verse, Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind, was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, Indeed, your left behind are being recorded, but they did not move. Al-Tirmidhi is the only one who transmitted it when he interpreted this noble verse on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Wazir, and then he said: It is hasan gharib from the hadith of al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sulayman ibn ‘Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqi, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Tarif - who is Ibn Shihab Abu Sufyan al-Sa’di - on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of him. It has been narrated via other than Al-Thawri’s chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: “Ibad bin Ziyad Al-Saji told us, Uthman bin Umar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id may God be pleased with him, who said: ‘The Banu Salamah complained to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about the distance between their stations and the mosque, so the verse, “And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind,” was revealed, so they stayed where they were.’ Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, ‘Abd Al-A’la told us, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in a similar manner. Ibn Abi Nujayh and others said on the authority of Mujahid, What they have put forth their deeds, and their traces he said: their steps with their feet, and this is what Al-Hasan and Qatadah said, and their traces meaning their steps. Qatadah said: If God, the Almighty, were to neglect anything about you, O son of Adam, He would have neglected what the winds erase of these traces, but He has counted all of the traces and deeds of the son of Adam until He counted this trace in what is from the obedience of God, the Almighty, or from His disobedience. So whoever among you is able to write down his trace in the obedience of God, the Almighty, let him do so. And there are hadiths with this meaning: The first hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, my father told us, al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The places around the mosque were deserted, so Banu Salamah wanted to move closer to the mosque. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said to them: I have heard that you want to move closer to the mosque. They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, we want to do that. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Banu Salamah, your dwellings record your footsteps, your dwellings record your footsteps. This is how Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sa’id al-Jariri and Kuhams ibn al-Hasan, both of them on the authority of Abu Nadrah, whose name was al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qat’ah al-Abdi, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him. The second hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Wasiti told us, Ishaq al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: Banu Salamah were in a part of Madinah, and they wanted to move closer to the mosque, so the verse, Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind, was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, Indeed, your left behind are being recorded, but they did not move. Al-Tirmidhi is the only one who transmitted it when he interpreted this noble verse on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Wazir, and then he said: It is hasan gharib from the hadith of al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sulayman ibn ‘Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqi, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Tarif - who is Ibn Shihab Abu Sufyan al-Sa’di - on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of him. It has been narrated via other than Al-Thawri’s chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: “Ibad bin Ziyad Al-Saji told us, Uthman bin Umar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id may God be pleased with him, who said: ‘The Banu Salamah complained to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about the distance between their stations and the mosque, so the verse, “And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind,” was revealed, so they stayed where they were.’ Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, ‘Abd Al-A’la told us, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in a similar manner. There is something strange about the mention of the revelation of this verse, and the entire Surah is Meccan, and God knows best.” The third hadith Ibn Jarir said: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubairi told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The homes of the Ansar were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move to the mosque, so the verse And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind was revealed. They said: We will remain where we are. This is how it was narrated, and there is no trace of a Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in it. Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Sa’id bin Abi Maryam, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Firyabi, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The homes of the Ansar were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move to the mosque, so the verse And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind was revealed, so they remained in their homes. The Fourth Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Huyayy ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both, who said: “A man died in Madinah, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed over him and said, ‘If only he had died somewhere other than his birthplace.’ A man among the people said, ‘Why, O Messenger of God?’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘If a man dies somewhere other than his birthplace, the distance from his birthplace to the place where his trace ends in Paradise will be measured for him.’” An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la and Ibn Majah on the authority of Harmalah, both on the authority of Ibn Wahb on the authority of Huyayy ibn Abdullah. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Abu Numailah told us, Al-Husayn told us on the authority of Thabit, who said: I walked with Anas may God be pleased with him and I walked quickly, so he took my hand and we walked slowly. When we finished the prayer, Anas said: I walked with Zayd ibn Thabit and I walked quickly. He said: O Anas, do you not know that traces are written? This statement does not contradict the first one, but rather it is a warning and indication of that by way of priority and more appropriate, because if these traces are written, then those in which there is an example of them, good or evil, are written by way of priority, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And everything We have recorded in a clear register meaning, all of creation is written in a written book, precisely recorded in a Preserved Tablet. The clear register here is the Mother of the Book, as stated by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. Likewise in the saying of the Almighty: The Day We will call every people with their register meaning with their register of deeds that will bear witness against them regarding what they did of good or evil, as the Almighty said: And the register will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forth and the Almighty said: “And the register will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is within it, and they will say, “Woe to us! What is this register that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has enumerated it?” And they will find what they did present. And your Lord does not wrong anyone.”
36:13: And God Almighty says: And, O Muhammad, present to your people who denied you, an example of the companions of the town, when there came to it the messengers. Ibn Ishaq said, according to what he heard from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Ka’b al-Ahbar, and Wahb ibn Munabbih: It is the city of Antioch, and there was a king there called Antiochus ibn Antiochus, who worshipped idols. So God sent three messengers to him, namely Sadiq, Sadooq, and Shalom, but he denied them. This is how it was narrated from Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and al-Zuhri that it was Antioch. Some imams questioned its being Antioch, as we will mention after the end of the story, God willing. God Almighty says: When We sent to them two, they denied them. That is, they rushed to deny them. So We reinforced them with a third. That is, We strengthened them and strengthened their support with a third messenger. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Wahb bin Sulayman on the authority of Shuayb al-Jubba’i who said: The names of the first two messengers were Simon and John, and the name of the third was Paul, and the village was Antioch. They said meaning to the people of that village We are messengers to you meaning from your Lord who created you, commanding you to worship Him alone, with no partner for Him. Abu al-Aaliyah said this. Qatada bin Di’amah claimed that they were the messengers of Jesus, peace be upon him, to the people of Antioch. They said, ‘You are only human beings like us’ meaning how can revelation be sent to you when you are human beings and we are human beings, so why shouldn’t revelation be sent to us like you? If you were messengers, you would have been angels. This is the doubt of many of the nations who deny God, as God Almighty has informed us about them in His saying, the Exalted: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, ‘Is it human beings who guide us?’ meaning they were amazed by that and denied it. And the Almighty said: “They said, ‘You are only human beings like us. You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. So bring us a clear authority.’” And the Almighty said, narrating from them in His saying, the Most High: And if you obeyed human beings like yourselves, indeed, you would then be losers. And the Almighty said: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, ‘Has God sent a human being as a messenger?’ For this reason, these people said: “You are only human beings like us, and the Most Gracious has not sent down anything. You are only lying.” They said, Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers to you. That is, their three messengers answered them, saying, “God knows that we are His messengers to you, and if we had lied to Him, He would not have exacted the most severe vengeance on us, but He will honor us and grant us victory over you, and you will know for whom the final outcome of the abode will be.” Like the Almighty’s saying: “Say, ‘Sufficient is God between me and you as a witness. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.’ But those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in God - it is they who are the losers.” And our responsibility is only to convey clearly. They said: Our responsibility is only to convey to you what we have been sent with, so if you obey, then happiness will be yours in this world and the hereafter, and if you do not respond, then you will know after that, and God knows best.

36:18: At that point, the people of the town said to them, We see no good in you, meaning, We have not seen any good in your faces during our lives. Qatada said, They say that if evil befalls us, it is only because of you. Mujahid said, "They say, 'No one like you has entered a town without its people being punished. 'If you do not desist, we will surely stone you.'" Qatada said, With stones. Mujahid said, With cursing. "And a painful punishment will touch you from Us," meaning, a severe punishment. Then their messengers said to them, "Your bad omen is with you, meaning, it will be returned to you, like the words of God about the people of Pharaoh, But when good comes to them, they say, 'This is from us.' But if evil befalls them, they see an evil omen in Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their bad omen is with God. The people of Salih said, We see an evil omen in you and those with you. He said, Your bad omen is with God. Qatada and Wahb ibn Munabbih said, Meaning, your deeds are with you." God the Almighty said: “And if good befalls them, they say, ‘This is from God.’ But if evil befalls them, they say, ‘This is from you.’ Say, ‘All is from God.’ So what is the matter with these people that they can hardly understand a statement?” And His Almighty saying: If you are reminded, then you are a transgressing people. That is, because We reminded you and commanded you to worship God alone and to devote worship to Him alone, you respond to us with these words and threaten and intimidate us. Rather, you are a transgressing people. Qatada said: That is, if We remind you of God, you take us as a bad omen. Rather, you are a transgressing people.

36:20: Ibn Ishaq said, as he was told by Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them, Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Wahb ibn Munabbih: The people of the village intended to kill their messengers, but a man from his people came running to them from the farthest part of the city, that is, to support them. They said: He was Habib, and he used to make ropes. He was a sick man who had been afflicted with leprosy. He used to give charity a lot, and he used to give away half of his earnings in charity. He was a righteous man. Ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of a man he named, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, or on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them, that the name of the companion of Yasin was Habib, and leprosy had afflicted him quickly. Ath-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, that his name was Habib ibn Sari. Shabib ibn Bishr said, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them, that the name of the companion of Yasin was Habib the carpenter, and his people killed him. As-Suddi said: He was a plasterer. Umar ibn al-Hakam said: He was a cobbler. Qatada said: He was worshipping in a cave there. He said, ‘O my people, follow the messengers,’ urging his people to follow the messengers who came to them. Follow those who ask you for no payment, meaning to convey the message and are guided in what they call you to of worshipping God alone, with no partner. And why should I not worship He who created me? “And to Him you will be returned,” meaning on the Day of Resurrection, when He will reward you for your deeds, whether good or evil. Should I take gods besides Him? This is a question of denial, rebuke, and rebuke. If the Most Gracious intends me harm, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me. He wished that God would inform his people of what he had witnessed of God's honor and what had attacked him. Ibn Abbas said: He advised his people during his life by saying, O my people, follow the messengers, and after his death by saying, I wish my people knew * that my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored ones. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, Because my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored ones, because of my faith in my Lord and my belief in the messengers. His intention is that if they had known what I had achieved in terms of this reward, recompense, and eternal bliss, it would have led them to follow the messengers. So may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him, for he was keen on guiding his people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ubaidullah told us, Ibn Jabir - he is Muhammad - told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik, meaning Ibn Umair, who said: Urwah bin Masoud Al-Thaqafi, may God be pleased with him, said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Send me to my people to call them to Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I fear that they will kill you. He said: If they found me asleep, they would not wake me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Go. So he went and passed by Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and said: I will bring you something tomorrow that will upset you. Thaqif became angry, and he said: O people of Thaqif, Al-Lat is not Al-Lat and Al-Uzza is not Al-Uzza. Submit and you will be safe. O people of the allies, Al-Uzza is not Al-Uzza and Al-Lat is not Al-Lat. Submit and you will be safe. He said that three times. A man shot him and struck his ankle and killed him. report of this reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: His example is like that of the companion of Yasin. He said: I wish my people knew * That my Lord has forgiven me. And make me among the honored ones. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Muammar bin Hazm that he narrated on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar that it was mentioned to him that Habib bin Zaid bin Asim, the brother of Banu Mazin bin An-Najjar, whom Musaylimah the Liar had cut into pieces in Al-Yamamah when he began to ask him about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he began to say to him: Do you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. Then he said: Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He said: I do not hear. Then Musaylimah, may God curse him, said to him: Do you hear this and not hear that? He said: Yes. So he began to cut him into pieces, piece by piece, and whenever he asked him, he did not say anything more until he died in his hands. When Ka’b was told his name was Habib, Ka’b said: By God, the companion of Jesus was named Habib. And the words of the Most High, Blessed and Exalted: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We have sent them down. The Most High informs us that He took revenge on his people after they killed him, out of His anger with them, because they denied His messengers and killed His friend. The Most High, Blessed and Exalted, mentions that He did not send down upon them, nor did He need to send down upon them an army of angels in order to destroy them. Rather, the matter was easier than that. Ibn Masoud said, as narrated by Ibn Ishaq on the authority of some of his companions, that he said about the verse: {And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We to send them down} meaning, We did not multiply them with multitudes. The matter would have been easier for Us than that. {It was only a single blast, and at once they were extinct} He said: So God destroyed that tyrannical king and destroyed the people of Antioch, so they were annihilated from the face of the earth, and not a remnant of them remained. It was also said, {And We did not send down} meaning, We did not send down angels upon nations when We destroyed them, but rather We would send upon them a punishment that would destroy them. It was also said that the meaning of the verse: {And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven} is another message to them. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. Qatadah said: By God, God did not rebuke his people after his killing. {It was only a single blast, and at once they were extinct} Ibn Jarir said: The first is more correct, because the message is not called an army. The commentators said. God the Almighty sent Gabriel, peace and blessings be upon him, to them. He took hold of the doorposts of their town, then shouted at them once, and they were all extinguished, no soul remaining in their bodies. Many of the predecessors have previously stated that this town is Antioch, and that these three were messengers from the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, peace and blessings be upon him, as stated by Qatada and others. This is what was not mentioned by any of the later commentators other than him. There is consideration of this from several aspects: One of them is that the apparent meaning of the story indicates that these were messengers from God Almighty, not from the Messiah, peace be upon him, as God Almighty said: “When We sent to them two, they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said, ‘Indeed, we are messengers to you.’ They said, ‘You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not sent down anything. You are only lying.’ They said, ‘Our Lord knows that we are messengers to you. And our duty is only to convey the clear message.’” If these people had been from the disciples, they would have said a phrase that would have been appropriate for them to be from the Messiah, peace be upon him. And God knows best. Then, if they had been messengers from the Messiah, they would not have said to them, You are not but human beings like us. The second is that the people of Antioch believed in the messengers of Christ to them, and they were the first city to believe in Christ, and for this reason it was among the Christians one of the four cities in which there was a Patriarchate, and they are: Jerusalem because it is the city of Christ, and Antioch because it was the first city to believe in Christ from the last of its people, and Alexandria because in it they agreed to take patriarchs, metropolitans, bishops, priests, deacons and monks, then Rome because it was the city of King Constantine who supported and established their religion, and when he built Constantinople they moved the Patriarchs from Rome to it, as mentioned by more than one of those who mentioned their histories, such as Saeed bin Batrik and others from the People of the Book and Muslims. So if it is established that Antioch was the first city to believe, then God Almighty mentioned that the people of this city denied His messengers and that He destroyed them with a single shout that extinguished them, and God knows best. Third The story of Antioch with the disciples, the companions of Christ, occurred after the Torah was revealed. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri may God be pleased with him and more than one of the early Muslims mentioned that after sending down the Torah, God, the Blessed and Exalted, did not destroy a single nation with a punishment that He sent upon them, but rather He ordered the believers after that to fight the polytheists. They mentioned this when God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: And We gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations. Based on this, it must be that this village mentioned in the Qur’an is a different village than Antioch, as was also stated by more than one of the early Muslims. Or Antioch, if its wording is preserved in this story, is another city other than this famous and well-known one, because it is not known that it was destroyed, neither in the Christian faith nor before that, and God, the Almighty, knows best. As for the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani: Al-Hussein bin Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Al-Hussein bin Abi Al-Sarri Al-Asqalani told us, Al-Hussein Al-Ashqar told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are three types of people who will race: the one who raced to Moses, peace be upon him, was Joshua bin Nun; the one who raced to Jesus, peace be upon him, the companion of Jesus; and the one who raced to Muhammad, peace be upon him, was Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him.” It is a rejected hadith, and is only known through the chain of transmission of Al-Hussein Al-Ashqar, who is a rejected Shiite, and God Almighty knows best what is correct.

They are the ones who say that there is a cycle among the eternity, and they are the ones who believe out of ignorance that they will return to this world, as they were in it. The meaning of this is like His, the Almighty, saying: And verily, all will be brought before Us in full for their deeds. The reciters differed in the pronunciation of this letter. Some of them read and verily, all will be brought before Us in full. According to him, in is for affirmation. Some of them stressed lama and made an negative, and lama means except, meaning, and there is no all except all brought before Us. The meaning of the two readings is the same, and God, the Almighty, knows best.
36:32: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: O regret for the servants meaning, O woe to the servants. Qatada said, O regret for the servants meaning, O regret of the servants for themselves for what they have wasted of God's command, and neglected in their duty to God. In some readings, it is: O regret of the servants for themselves. The meaning of this is, "O regret and remorse for them on the Day of Resurrection when they witness the punishment, for how they denied God's messengers and disobeyed God's command. For in this world, the deniers among them were "There came to them no messenger but they mocked him." That is, they denied him and mocked him and glorified the truth with which he was sent. Then God the Almighty said: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them? That to them they will not be returned? That is, have they not learned a lesson from those who denied the Messengers whom God destroyed before them? How they will not have a return to this world or a return? And the matter was not as many of their ignorant and wicked ones claimed when they said: It is only our worldly life; we die and live. They are the ones who say that there is a cycle among the eternity, and they are the ones who believe out of ignorance that they will return to this world, as they were in it. So God the Blessed and Exalted refuted their falsehood, saying: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them? That to them they will not be returned. And the Almighty said: And verily, all will be brought before Us in full. That is, all the nations past and future will be brought before Us for judgment on the Day of Resurrection before God, the Almighty, and He will reward them for all their deeds, both good and bad. The meaning of this is like His, the Almighty, saying: And verily, all will be brought before Us in full for their deeds. The reciters differed in the pronunciation of this letter. Some of them read and verily, all will be brought before Us in full. According to him, in is for affirmation. Some of them stressed lama and made an negative, and lama means except, meaning, and there is no all except all brought before Us. The meaning of the two readings is the same, and God, the Almighty, knows best.
36:33: God the Most High says: And a sign for them meaning an indication to them of the existence of the Creator, His perfect power, and His revival of the dead, is the dead land meaning if it is dead and lifeless, with nothing of vegetation in it, then when God the Most High sends down water upon it, it quivers and swells and produces every beautiful pair. For this reason God the Most High said: We revived it and brought forth from it grain, from which they eat meaning We made it a provision for them and their livestock and placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused springs to gush forth therein meaning We made therein flowing rivers in places where they need to eat from its fruit. When He bestowed His favor upon His creation by creating crops for them, He followed it up by mentioning the fruits and their variety and types. And the saying of the Most High: And what their hands have made means that all of that is only from the mercy of God Almighty to them, not by their effort or their toil or by their own power and strength. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Qatadah said: This is why the Most High said: Then will they not then be grateful? meaning why will they not thank Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon them, which are countless and innumerable. Ibn Jarir chose - indeed, he was certain of it, and no one else narrated it except as a possibility - that what in the saying of the Most High: And what their hands have made means that, meaning that they may eat from its fruit and from what their hands have made, meaning that they planted and erected it. He said: And it is like that in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him: So that they may eat from its fruit and from what their hands have made, will they not then be grateful? Then the Most High said: Glory be to Him who created in pairs all things that the earth grows meaning crops, fruits, and plants and from themselves so He made them male and female and from that which they do not know meaning from various creatures that they do not know, as the Most High said: And of everything We created pairs that you may remember.

36:37: God the Almighty says: And among the proofs for them of His great power, the Blessed and Exalted is He, is that He created the night and the day, this with its darkness and this with its light, and made them alternate, one coming and the other going, and the other going and the other coming, as God the Almighty said: The night overtakes the day, pursuing it swiftly. That is why God the Almighty said here: “And a sign for them is the night. We remove from it the day,” meaning We cut it off from it, so it goes and the night comes. That is why God the Blessed and Exalted said: Then they are in darkness, as came in the hadith: When the night comes from here and the day departs from here and the sun sets, then the fasting person has broken his fast. This is what appears from the verse. Qatadah claimed that it is like God the Almighty’s saying: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night. Ibn Jarir weakened Qatadah’s statement here, and said: The meaning of merging is taking from this into that, and this is not what is intended in this verse. What Ibn Jarir said is true. And His Most High saying: “And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the determination of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.” Concerning the meaning of His saying: to its resting place, there are two opinions. One of them is that what is meant is its spatial resting place, which is under the Throne, which is next to the Earth on that side. And wherever it is, it is under the Throne, along with all of the creation, because it is its roof. And it is not a pulley, as many of the masters of astronomy claim. Rather, it is a dome with pillars carried by the angels, and it is above the world, which is next to the heads of the people. So when the sun is in the dome of the heavens at noon, it is closest to the Throne. So when it turns in its fourth orbit to face this station, which is the time of midnight, it becomes farthest from the Throne. At that time, it prostrates and asks permission to rise, as came in the hadiths. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu`aym told us, Al-A`mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque at sunset, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Dharr, do you know where the sun sets? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne. This is what God Almighty said: “And the sun runs to a resting place. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.” Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi narrated to us, Wakee’ narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the words of God Almighty: ‘And the sun runs to its resting place.’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Its resting place is beneath the Throne.’” This is how he mentioned it here, and he included it in many places, and the rest of the group, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us from al-A’mash from Ibrahim al-Taymi from his father from Abu Dharr, who said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque when the sun set. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O Abu Dharr, do you know where the sun goes?’ I said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It goes until it prostrates before its Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, and asks permission to return, and it is given permission. It is as if it has been told to return from where you came. So it returns to its rising place, and that is its resting place.’ Then he recited: ‘And the sun runs to its resting place.’” Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from al-A’mash from Ibrahim al-Taymi from his father from Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Dharr when the sun set: ‘Do you know where it goes?’ I said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne, and asks permission, and it is given permission. It is about to prostrate, but it is not accepted from it. And it asks permission, but it is not given permission. It is told to return from where you came, and it rises from…’” Its setting, so that is what God Almighty said: “And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.” Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both, who said regarding the verse: {And the sun runs to its resting place}, that he said: The sun rises and is held back by the sins of the children of Adam, until when it sets, it greets God and prostrates and asks permission to go, until when it sets on the day it greets God and prostrates and asks permission to go, but it is not given permission. So it says, The journey is far, and if I am not given permission, I will not reach it. So it is detained for as long as God wills it to be detained, then it is told, Go up from where it set. He said: From that day until the Day of Resurrection, faith will not benefit a soul if it did not believe before, or earn good through its faith. It was said: What is meant by its resting place is the end of its journey, which is its maximum height in the sky in the summer, which is its zenith, then its maximum depth in the winter, which is its lowest point. The second opinion is that what is meant by its resting place is the end of its journey, which is the Day of Resurrection. Its journey will be nullified, its movement will stop, and it will be rolled up, and this world will reach its end, and this is its temporal resting place. Qatada said, its resting place means its time and its term that it will not exceed. It was said that what is meant is that it will continue to move during its summer rising for a period that does not exceed it, then it will move during the winter rising for a period that does not exceed it. This is narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, may God be pleased with them both. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them read: And the sun runs to its resting place, meaning it has no rest or stillness, rather it moves night and day, never slackening or stopping, as God the Most High said: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, constantly pursuing their courses, meaning they will never slacken or stop until the Day of Resurrection. That is the decree of the Almighty, meaning the One who does not contradict or oppose, the Knower of all movements and stillness. He has determined that and set its time in a manner in which there is no difference or contradiction, as God the Almighty said: “He who splits the dawn and makes the night for rest and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing.” Thus He concluded the verse, Ha Mim, as-Sajdah, with His saying, That is the decree of the Almighty, the Knowing. Then the Almighty said: And the moon - We have determined for it phases. That is, We made it move in a different path by which we can determine the passage of months, just as the sun is used to determine the night and day, as the Almighty said: “They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj.’” God the Almighty said: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account (10:17). He also said: “And We made the night and the day two signs, and We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible - that you may seek bounty from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and account. And We have detailed all things in detail” (10:17). He made the sun have its own light and the moon has its own light, and He made a difference between the movements of these and those. The sun rises every day and sets at the end of it with one light, but it moves in its risings and settings in summer and winter, because of that the day lengthens and the night shortens, then the night lengthens and the day shortens. He made its power by the day, so it is a diurnal planet. As for the moon, its phases are determined. It rises on the first night of the month, small and with little light, then its light increases on the second night and it rises in status. Then every time it rises, its light increases, even though it is borrowed from the sun, until its light is complete on the fourteenth night. Then it begins to decrease until the end of the month until it becomes like an old palm branch. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: It is the base of the cluster. Mujahid said: The old cluster, meaning the dry cluster, means Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him means the base of the cluster of dates when it is old, dry and bent, and others said the same. Then after this God makes it new at the beginning of the next month. The Arabs name every three nights of the month based on the moon. They call the first three Gharar, and those after them Naql, and those after them are nine, because the last of them is the ninth, and those after them are ten, because the first of them are ten, and those after them are Al-Baydh, because the moon’s light is in them until the end of them, and those after them are Dar’, plural of Dar’a, because the first of them is black due to the moon being late in the first of them, and from this comes the word Dar’a, which is the one with a black head. After them are three Dhalam, then three Hanadis, three Dadadi, and three Muhaq because the moon or the month is extinguished in them. Abu Ubaidah may God be pleased with him did not approve of the nine and the ten. This is what he said in the book Gharib Al-Musannaf. And the saying of God the Most High: The sun shall not overtake the moon. Mujahid said: Each of them has a limit that they cannot exceed or fall short of. When the authority of one comes, that one goes, and when the authority of one goes, the authority of another comes. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of al-Hasan regarding the saying of God the Most High: The sun shall not overtake the moon, he said: That is on the night of the crescent moon. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak that he said: The wind has wings, and the moon seeks refuge in a covering of water. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid on the authority of Abu Salih: The light of one does not overtake the light of the other, nor does the light of the other. Ikrimah said regarding the saying of God the Most High: The sun shall not overtake the moon, meaning that each of them has an authority! So the sun shall not rise at night. God the Almighty says: {Nor does the night outstrip the day} meaning: It is not right that when there is night, there should be another night until there is day. The sun’s power is in the day and the moon’s power is in the night. Ad-Dahhak said: The night does not go from here until the day comes from here, and he pointed with his hand to the east. Mujahid said: {Nor does the night outstrip the day} they pursue one another hastily, one peeling off the other. The meaning of this is that there is no interval between the night and the day, rather one follows the other without delay or slackness, because they are subjugated and constantly pursuing one another hastily. God the Almighty said: And each, in an orbit, is floating. He means the night and the day, the sun and the moon. They all float, that is, they revolve in the orbit of the heavens. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ata’ Al-Khurasani. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: In an orbit between the heaven and the earth. It was also narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and it is very strange, indeed objectionable. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and more than one of the early Muslims said: In an orbit like the orbit of a spindle. Mujahid said: “An orbit is like the iron of a millstone or the orbit of a spindle. The spindle does not rotate except with it, and it does not rotate except with it.”

36:45: God Almighty says, informing about the persistence of the polytheists in their error and misguidance and their lack of concern for their past sins and what they will face on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:And when it is said to them, ‘Fear what is before you and what is behind you,’ Mujahid said: Of sins. Others said the opposite, that you may receive mercy. That is, perhaps by your fearing that, God will have mercy on you and secure you from His punishment. The meaning of the statement is that they do not respond to that, but rather turn away from it. God Almighty sufficed with His statement: And there does not come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord, that is, about monotheism and the truthfulness of the messengers, except that they turn away from it, that is, they do not contemplate it, nor accept it, nor benefit from it. God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, ‘Spend from what God has provided you,’ meaning, when they are commanded to spend from what God has provided them on the poor and needy among the Muslims, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, meaning, about the poor who believed, meaning, they say to those among the believers who commanded them to spend, arguing with them about what they were commanded to do, Should we feed those whom, if God willed, He could feed? meaning, these are the ones you commanded us to spend on. You are in clear error, meaning, in your commanding us to do that. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that it is from the words of God the Almighty to the disbelievers when they debated with the believers and responded to them, so He said to them, You are in clear error, and there is a problem with this, and God knows best.

36:48: God Almighty tells us about the disbelievers’ rejection of the Hour in their saying: When will this promise come to pass? “Those who do not believe in it hasten it.” God Almighty said: They await only a single blast that will seize them while they are disputing. That is, they await only a single blast, and this, God knows best, is the blast of terror. The trumpet will be blown with a blast of terror, and people will be in their markets and livelihoods disputing and arguing as is their custom. While they are like this, God Almighty commands Israfil to blow the trumpet with a blast that he will prolong and extend, so that no one will remain on the face of the earth except that he will listen attentively and raise his hand, which is the side of the neck, listening to the sound from the sky. Then those who are present will be driven to the place of resurrection with fire surrounding them from all sides. For this reason, God Almighty said: And they will not be able to make a will, that is, regarding what they own, the matter is more important than that, nor will they return to their families. There are traces and hadiths here that we have mentioned elsewhere, then After this will be the blast of the trumpet, by which all living beings will die except the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Then after that will be the blast of resurrection.

36:51: This is the third blast, which is the blast of resurrection and rising from the graves. That is why God the Almighty said: Then at once they will hasten from the graves to their Lord. "Hashing" means walking quickly, as God the Almighty said: "The Day they emerge from the graves quickly, as if they were, toward an idol, hastening. They will say, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds?'" They mean their graves, which they believed in this worldly life that they would not be raised from. But when they witness what they denied in the place of assembly, "They will say, 'Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds?'" This does not negate their torment in their graves, because in relation to what comes after it, it is as severe as sleep. Ubayy ibn Ka'b may God be pleased with him, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: They will sleep a sleep before the resurrection. Qatada said: “That will be between the two blasts, and that is why they will say, ‘Who has raised us from our place of sleep?’ When they say that, the believers will answer them. More than one of the early Muslims said this: ‘This is what the Most Gracious promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.’” Al-Hasan said: The angels will answer them with that, and there is no contradiction, since the combination is possible, and God Almighty knows best. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid said: All of them are from the saying of the infidels, Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds? This is what the Most Gracious promised, and the messengers spoke the truth. Ibn Jarir transmitted it, and he chose the first, which is more correct, because of the saying of God, the Most High, in al-Saffat 37:And they will say, ‘Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense! This is the Day of Separation which you used to deny.’ And God, the Most High, said: “And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear that they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour. Thus were they deluded. And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, ‘You did remain according to the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.’ This is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.” And the Almighty’s saying: It will be only a single blast, and at once they will all be brought before Us is like His saying, the Almighty: It will be only a single blast, and at once they will all be in the dark. And He, the Majestic and Sublime, said: And the Hour will not come but as the twinkling of an eye, or even nearer. And He, the Majestic and Sublime, said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with praise of Him, and you will think that you had remained only a little. That is, We will only command them with one command, and at once they will all be brought before Us. So today no soul will be wronged at all, that is, of its deeds, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.

36:59: God Almighty says, informing us of what will happen to the unbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, that He commanded them to be distinguished, meaning that they will be distinguished from the believers in their situation, as God Almighty says: And the Day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated others with God, ‘Stay where you are, you and your associates.’ So We shall separate them. And God Almighty says: And the Day the Hour appears, on that Day they will be divided. “On that Day they will be split apart,” meaning they will be split into two groups. Gather together those who did wrong, their spouses, and that which they worshipped * besides God, and guide them to the path of Hellfire. God the Almighty says: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - for indeed, he is to you a clear enemy? This is a rebuke from God the Almighty to the disbelievers among the children of Adam, who obeyed Satan, who is their clear enemy, and disobeyed the Most Gracious, who created them and provided for them. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “And that you worship Me. This is a straight path.” That is, I commanded you in this world to disobey Satan, and I commanded you to worship Me, and this is the straight path, but you took a different path and followed Satan in what he commanded you. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And he has certainly led astray from among you a great multitude. It is said: a mountain with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam, and it is said with a damma on the jim and the ba’ and a soft lam, and some of them make the ba’ sukoon, and what is meant by that is a great multitude of creation, as stated by Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. God the Almighty says: Did you not reason? That is, did you not have reason in disobeying your Lord in what He commanded you to worship Him alone, with no partner, and in following Satan? Ibn Jurayj said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abdur-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, “that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God the Almighty will command Hell, and a luminous, dark neck will emerge from it, saying: ‘Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy - and that you worship Me. This is a straight path. And he has led astray many a generation from among you. Did you not reason? This is Hell, which you were promised.’ ‘And separate yourselves today, O criminals.’” So the people will separate themselves and kneel, and it is about this that God the Almighty says: “And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.”

He said: God Almighty will forgive him his sins and conceal them from him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Shaybah Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Abi Shaybah told us, Munjab bin Al-Harith Al-Tamimi told us, Abu Amir Al-Azdi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubayd Al-Maktab, on the authority of Al-Fudayl bin Amr, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he laughed until his molars were visible. Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know why I laugh? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: From the servant’s argument with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He will say: O Lord, did you not save me from injustice? He will say: Yes. He will say: I will not accept against me except a witness from myself. He will say: Your own self is sufficient as a reckoner against you today, and the noble scribes are witnesses. Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will be told: Speak, and they will speak of his deeds. Then he will be left alone to speak, and he will say: Far be it from you and be crushed, for it was for you that I struggled. Muslim and Al-Nasa’i narrated it, both of them on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Nadr on the authority of Abu An-Nadr, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with it. Then al-Nasa’i said: I do not know of anyone who narrated this hadith on the authority of Sufyan other than al-Ashja’i, and it is a strange hadith, and God knows best. This is what he said. It was previously narrated by Abu Amir Abd al-Malik ibn Amr al-Asadi, who is al-Aqdi, on the authority of Sufyan. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Bahz ibn Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will be called Mufaddal over your mouths, so the first thing that will be asked about one of you will be his thigh and his shoulder. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on his authority. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the long hadith of the Resurrection, in which he said: “Then he will meet the third one and say: Who are you? He will say: I am your servant. I believed in you and your prophet and your book, and I fasted and prayed and gave charity, and he praised you as much as he could.” He said: “It will be said to him: Shall we not send our witness against you?” He said: “So he will think in himself about who will testify against him, and his mouth will be sealed and his thigh will be told: Speak.” He said: So his thigh, flesh, and bones will speak about what he used to do, and that is the hypocrite, and that is so that he may excuse himself, and that is the one with whom God Almighty is angry. And it was narrated by Muslim and Abu Dawood from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah in full. Then Ibn Abi Hatim may God have mercy on him said: My father told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, Damdam ibn Zar’ah told us, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir may God be pleased with him, “that he heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: ‘The first bone of man to speak on the Day when mouths are sealed will be his left thigh.’” Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Awf, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ayyash, with a similar chain of narration. Imam Ahmad may God have mercy on him authenticated its chain of narration, saying: Al-Hakam ibn Nafi’ told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Damdam ibn Zar’ah, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd al-Hadrami, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir may God be pleased with him, “that he heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: ‘The first bone of man to speak on the Day when mouths are sealed will be his left thigh.’” Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Burdah said: Abu Musa - he is al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him - said: The believer will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection, and his Lord will show him his deeds between him and Him, and he will confess and say: Yes, O Lord, I did, I did, I did. He said: God Almighty will forgive him his sins and conceal them from him. He said: There is no creature on earth that sees any of those sins and his good deeds are apparent, and he would like all people to see them. The disbeliever and the hypocrite will be called to account, and his Lord will show him his deeds, but he will deny them and say: O Lord, by Your glory, this angel wrote for me what I did not do. The angel will say to him: Did you not know such and such on such and such a day in such and such a place? He says: No, by Your glory, O Lord, I did not do that. So when he does that, God will seal his mouth. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him, said: I think the first part of his mouth to speak will be the right thigh. Then he recited: This Day We will seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn. God the Almighty said: {And if We willed, We could have blinded their eyes and they would race along the path. How could they see?} Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him in its interpretation: He says, And if We willed, We could have led them astray from guidance, so how could they be guided? And he said once: We blinded them. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: If God willed, He could have blinded their eyes and made them blind, wandering around. Al-Suddi said: He says, And if We willed, We could have blinded their sight. Mujahid, Abu Salih, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said: And they would race along the path, meaning the road. Ibn Zayd said: What is meant by the path here is the truth, so how could they see when We have blinded their eyes. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him: And how could they see means they cannot see the truth. And the Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have transformed them in their places. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: We would have destroyed them. Al-Suddi said: It means that someone other than Us created them. Abu Salih said: We would have made them stones. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatadah said: We would have made them sit on their feet. For this reason, the Almighty said: Then they were unable to proceed meaning forward nor return to backward, but rather they remain in one state, neither advancing nor falling back.

That is, this is the Hell which the messengers warned you about, but you denied them. Enter it today for what you used to disbelieve. As God the Almighty said: The Day they are summoned to the fire of Hell, it will be summoned, ‘This is the Fire which you used to deny.’ Is this magic, or do you not see?
