36:68: God Almighty tells us about the son of Adam that the longer his life, the more he returns to weakness after strength, and to inability after energy, as He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: “God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.” And He, the Almighty, said: And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age so that he does not know, after having known, a thing. What is meant by this - and God knows best - is informing us that this abode is an abode of passing and transition, not an abode of permanence and stability. For this reason, the Almighty said: Do they not then reason? That is, do they not think with their minds about the beginning of their creation, then their becoming gray hair, then old age, so that they may know that they were created for another abode that will not pass away, from which there is no transition, and from which there is no escape, and that is the abode of the Hereafter. And the saying of God the Blessed and Most High: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for it. God the Almighty says, informing about His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that He did not teach him poetry. And it was not befitting for him, meaning it was not in his nature, so he did not excel at it, nor did he like it, nor was his nature dictated by it. For this reason, it was reported that “he, peace and blessings be upon him, would not memorize a verse with a regular meter, but if he was asked to recite it, he would skip it or not complete it.” Abu Zur’ah al-Razi said: Ismail ibn Mujalid told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, that he said: Abdul Muttalib did not give birth, male or female, without reciting poetry, except for the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. Ibn Asakir mentioned him in the biography of Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, who was eaten by the lion in Zarqa. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Salamah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who is Al-Basri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite this verse: Islam and gray hair are enough to deter a person Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God Gray hair and Islam are enough to prevent a person Abu Bakr or Omar, may God be pleased with them, said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. God Almighty says: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. And thus Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Al-Dala’il: “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Abbas bin Mirdas Al-Sulami, may God be pleased with him: You are the one who said: Do you make my loot and the loot of the slaves between Al-Aqra’ and Uyaynah? He said: It is only Uyaynah and Al-Aqra’. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are all the same, meaning in meaning, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And God knows best. Al-Suhayli mentioned in Al-Rawdh Al-Anf that this inversion and postponement that occurred in his speech, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse is a strange occasion, the gist of which is the honor of Al-Aqra’ bin Habis over Uyaynah bin Badr Al-Fazari because he apostatized during the days of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, unlike that, and God knows best. And thus Al-Umawi narrated in his Maghazi, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked among the dead on the day of Badr and he was saying, ‘We split a crown.’” So Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said, completing the verse: From men who were dear to us, but they were disobedient and unjust This is by some Arab poets in a poem of his which is about enthusiasm. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us: Mughirah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: “Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about report, he would recite the verse of Tarafa: ‘And he who has no provision will bring you report.’” This is how Al-Nasa’i narrated it in Al-Yawm wal-Laylah on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on her authority. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Shuraih bin Hani’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, likewise. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Yusuf bin Musa told us, Usamah told us, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would recite from poetry: ‘And he who has no provision will bring you report.’” Then he said: Others than Za’idah narrated it on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her. This is in the poetry of Tarafa bin Al-Abd in his famous Mu’allaqa, and this is the beginning of what is mentioned: Days will show you what you were ignorant of, and report will come to you from someone you did not know. And he brings you report from someone you never told anyone about and for whom you never set a time to meet. Saeed bin Abi Aruba said on the authority of Qatada: It was said to Aisha may God be pleased with her: Did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite any poetry? She may God be pleased with her said: It was the most hated speech to him, except that he (peace and blessings be upon him) would recite the verse of the brother of Banu Qais, making its beginning its end and its end its beginning. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: This is not how it is, O Messenger of God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: By God, I am not a poet and it is not appropriate for me to do so. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: It reached me that Aisha may God be pleased with her was asked: Did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite any poetry? She may God be pleased with her said: No, except for the verse of Tarafa. Days will show you what you were ignorant of, and report will come to you from someone you did not know. “So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) began to say: ‘Whoever is not provided with report,’ Abu Bakr said: ‘That is not how it is.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘I am not a poet, and it is not appropriate for me to be.’” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Hafs Omar bin Ahmed bin Naim, the agent of Al-Muttaqi in Baghdad, told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Hilal Al-Nahwi Al-Dharee’ told us, Ali bin Amr Al-Ansari told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) never collected a verse of poetry except one verse. Be optimistic about what you desire and it will happen, for it is rarely said that something was, except that it came true. I asked our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, about this hadith, and he said: It is rejected, and neither Sheikh al-Hakim nor al-Dharee’ knew it. It is proven in the Sahih that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited on the day of digging the trench the verses of Abdullah bin Rawahah, may God be pleased with him, but according to the words of his companions, may God be pleased with them, for they were reciting rajaz poetry while they were digging, saying: If it weren't for you, we wouldn't have been guided, believed, or prayed. So send down tranquility upon us and plant firmly our feet if we meet [the enemy]. Those who have transgressed against us, if they wanted to cause strife, we would refuse. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would raise his voice, saying, Our father, and prolong it. This has also been narrated with a sukoon in the two Sahihs. And it has also been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Hunayn while he was riding the mule, advancing towards the enemy’s throats: I am the prophet, there is no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib But they said that this happened by chance without intending to do so, rather it just came out of the tongue without intending it. Likewise, what was established in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jundub bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a cave, and he cut his finger, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you nothing but a finger that bled and in the way of God did not find anything? And when God Almighty says, “except for a small amount,” there will be a recitation: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot. What servant of yours has not suffered? All of this does not contradict the fact that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not know poetry, nor did he deserve it, for God, the Most High, taught him the Noble Qur’an, “which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it. It is sent down by One Wise and Praiseworthy.” It is not poetry, as claimed by a group of ignorant infidels among the Quraysh, nor is it divination, nor is it fabricated, nor is it effective magic, as various misguided sayings and ignorant opinions have varied regarding it. His (peace and blessings of God be upon him) nature rejected the art of poetry, both by nature and by law, as narrated by Abu Dawud, who said: Ubaydullah bin Umar told us, Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Shurahbil bin Yazid al-Ma’afari told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Rafi’ al-Tanukhi, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Amr may God be pleased with them both say: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: ‘I do not care what I am given if I drink an antidote, or wear an amulet, or write poetry on my own.’” Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it. Imam Ahmad may God have mercy on him said: Abdur-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us on the authority of Al-Aswad ibn Shaiban on the authority of Abu Nawfal who said: I asked Aisha may God be pleased with her: Was poetry permissible to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him)? She said: It was the most hated speech to him. And he said on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) liked comprehensive supplications, and he would leave what was in between. And Abu Dawud said: Abu Al-Walid At-Tayalisi narrated to us: Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): For the inside of one of you to be filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry. He is the only one who narrated it from this source, and its chain of transmission meets the criteria of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Qaz’ah bin Suwaid al-Bahili told us, on the authority of As bin Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani H, and al-Ashib told us, on the authority of Abu Asim, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath, on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever recites a verse of poetry after the last ‘Isha’ prayer, his prayer will not be accepted that night.’” This is a strange hadith from this perspective, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it. What is meant by that is its composition, not its recitation, and God knows best. However, poetry is what is permissible, which is the satire of the polytheists that the poets of Islam were involved in, such as Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, Ka’b bin Malik, Abdullah bin Rawahah, and their likes and peers, may God be pleased with them all. Some of it contains wisdom, sermons, and etiquette, as is found in the poetry of a group of people from the pre-Islamic era, including Umayyah bin Abi al-Salt, about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved. Some of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, recited poetry to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. One hundred verses, he says after each verse Heyyah meaning he tastes it, and he increases it. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, and Abdullah ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Indeed, there is magic in eloquence, and in poetry there is wisdom. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And We did not teach him poetry, meaning Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not teach him poetry. Nor is it befitting for it, meaning nor is it suitable for it. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur’an, meaning what we have been taught is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur’an, meaning it is clear, evident, and distinct for whoever contemplates and ponders it. For this reason, God the Almighty said: To warn whoever is alive, meaning this clear Qur’an warns every living being on the face of the earth, like His statement: To warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. And God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in it of the parties - the Fire is his promised destination. Only he who has a living heart and enlightened insight will benefit from its warning, as Qatada said: A living heart is a living sight. Ad-Dahhak said, meaning rational, and the word will come true against the disbelievers, meaning it is a mercy for the believers and an argument against the disbelievers.

Ibn Asakir mentioned him in the biography of Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, who was eaten by the lion in Zarqa. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Shuraih bin Hani’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, likewise. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Yusuf bin Musa told us, Usamah told us, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) would recite from poetry: ‘And he who has no provision will bring you report.’” Then he said: Others than Za’idah narrated it on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her. This is in the poetry of Tarafa bin Al-Abd in his famous Mu’allaqa, and this is the beginning of what is mentioned: Days will show you what you were ignorant of, and report will come to you from someone you did not know. And he brings you report from someone you never told anyone about and for whom you never set a time to meet. Saeed bin Abi Aruba said on the authority of Qatada: It was said to Aisha may God be pleased with her: Did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite any poetry? She may God be pleased with her said: It was the most hated speech to him, except that he (peace and blessings be upon him) would recite the verse of the brother of Banu Qais, making its beginning its end and its end its beginning. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: This is not how it is, O Messenger of God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: By God, I am not a poet and it is not appropriate for me to do so. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and this is its wording. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: It reached me that Aisha may God be pleased with her was asked: Did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recite any poetry? She may God be pleased with her said: No, except for the verse of Tarafa. Be optimistic about what you desire and it will happen, for it is rarely said that something was, except that it came true. And when God Almighty says, “except for a small amount,” there will be a recitation: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot. What servant of yours has not suffered? His (peace and blessings of God be upon him) nature rejected the art of poetry, both by nature and by law, as narrated by Abu Dawud, who said: Ubaydullah bin Umar told us, Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Saeed bin Abi Ayyub told us, Shurahbil bin Yazid al-Ma’afari told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Rafi’ al-Tanukhi, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Amr may God be pleased with them both say: “I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: ‘I do not care what I am given if I drink an antidote, or wear an amulet, or write poetry on my own.’” Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it. Imam Ahmad may God have mercy on him said: Abdur-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us on the authority of Al-Aswad ibn Shaiban on the authority of Abu Nawfal who said: I asked Aisha may God be pleased with her: Was poetry permissible to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him)? She said: It was the most hated speech to him. And he said on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) liked comprehensive supplications, and he would leave what was in between. And Abu Dawud said: Abu Al-Walid At-Tayalisi narrated to us: Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): For the inside of one of you to be filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry. He is the only one who narrated it from this source, and its chain of transmission meets the criteria of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Qaz’ah bin Suwaid al-Bahili told us, on the authority of As bin Mukhallad, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani H, and al-Ashib told us, on the authority of Abu Asim, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath, on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever recites a verse of poetry after the last ‘Isha’ prayer, his prayer will not be accepted that night.’” This is a strange hadith from this perspective, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it. What is meant by that is its composition, not its recitation, and God knows best. However, poetry is what is permissible, which is the satire of the polytheists that the poets of Islam were involved in, such as Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, Ka’b bin Malik, Abdullah bin Rawahah, and their likes and peers, may God be pleased with them all. Some of it contains wisdom, sermons, and etiquette, as is found in the poetry of a group of people from the pre-Islamic era, including Umayyah bin Abi al-Salt, about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved. Some of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, recited poetry to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. One hundred verses, he says after each verse Heyyah meaning he tastes it, and he increases it. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, and Abdullah ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Indeed, there is magic in eloquence, and in poetry there is wisdom. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And We did not teach him poetry, meaning Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not teach him poetry. Nor is it befitting for it, meaning nor is it suitable for it. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur’an, meaning what we have been taught is nothing but a reminder and a clear Qur’an, meaning it is clear, evident, and distinct for whoever contemplates and ponders it. For this reason, God the Almighty said: To warn whoever is alive, meaning this clear Qur’an warns every living being on the face of the earth, like His statement: To warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. And God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in it of the parties - the Fire is his promised destination. Only he who has a living heart and enlightened insight will benefit from its warning, as Qatada said: A living heart is a living sight. Ad-Dahhak said, meaning rational, and the word will come true against the disbelievers, meaning it is a mercy for the believers and an argument against the disbelievers.

36:71: The Almighty mentions the blessings He bestowed upon His creation from these blessings that He subjected to them, so they own them. Qatada said: able to do so, meaning He made them subjugate them while they are submissive to them, and do not resist them. Likewise, if the train were a hundred camels or more, they would all move at the pace of the young one. And the Almighty’s saying: And from them they ride and from them they eat meaning from them is what they ride on in journeys and on which they carry heavy loads to all directions and regions and from them they eat if they wish and slaughter and butcher and for them therein are benefits meaning from their wool, fur and hair as furniture and provisions for a time and as drink meaning from their milk and urine for those who seek medical treatment and the like. God the Almighty says: And they are for them a present host. Mujahid said: meaning, at the reckoning. He means that these idols will be gathered together on the Day of Resurrection and present when their worshippers are held to account, so that this will be more expressive of their grief and more indicative of their argument against them. 36:77: Mujahid, Ikrimah, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, al-Suddi, and Qatadah said: “Ubayy ibn Khalaf, may God curse him, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in his hand was a rotten bone, which he was crumbling and scattering in the air, and he was saying: O Muhammad, do you claim that God will resurrect this? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, God Almighty will cause you to die, then He will resurrect you, then He will gather you to the Fire.” And these verses were revealed at the end of Ya Sin: Does man not see that We created him from a sperm-drop? until the end of them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junaid narrated to us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ narrated to us, Uthman bin Saeed Al-Zayyat narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “Al-Aas bin Wa’il took a bone from the plain of Batha’ and crumbled it in his hand, then he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Will God bring this to life after I see it?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes, God will cause you to die, then bring you to life, then cause you to enter Hell.’” He said: And the verses were revealed at the end of Ya-Seen. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ya’qub bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, and he mentioned him but did not mention Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Abdullah bin Ubayy came with a bone and crushed it, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. This is strange, because the Surah is Meccan and Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul was only in Medina. In any case, whether these verses were revealed about Ubayy bin Half or Al-As bin Wa’il or both of them, they are general for everyone who denies the Resurrection. The definite article in the words of God Almighty: Has not man considered refers to the genus and includes everyone who denies the Resurrection that We created him from a sperm-drop, then at once he is a clear adversary. That is, has not the one who denies the Resurrection used the beginning as evidence for the return? God began the creation of man from a lineage of despised water, so He created him from something insignificant, weak, and despised, as God Almighty said: Did We not create you from a despised water? Then We placed him in a secure lodging, for a known term? And God Almighty said: Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture. That is, from a sperm-drop of dispersed mixtures. So is He not able to To bring him back after his death. As Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Jarir told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Maysarah told me, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Bishr bin Jahash, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat one day into his hand, then placed his finger on it, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty said: Son of Adam, how can you outstrip Me when I created you from something like this, until, when I proportioned you and made you equal, you walked between your two garments, and the earth was slow from you. You gathered and withheld until, when you reached the collarbones, I said: ‘Shall I give charity?’ But when is the time for charity?” It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun on the authority of Jarir ibn Uthman on his authority. That is why God the Almighty said: “And he has presented to Us an example and forgotten his own creation. He says, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?’” That is, he doubted that God the Almighty, the One with the great power who created the heavens and the earth, would bring back the decayed bodies and bones. He forgot himself, and that God the Almighty created him from nothingness into existence. So he knew about himself something greater than what he doubted, denied, and rejected. That is why God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘He will give them life who produced them the first time. And He is Knowing of all creation.’” That is, He knows the bones in all parts of the earth and its regions, where they went and where they were scattered and torn apart. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Rab’i, who said: Uqba bin Amr said to Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with them both: Will you not tell us what you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: I heard him, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A man was dying, and when he despaired of life, he advised his family: ‘When I die, gather for me a large amount of firewood, then light a fire in it until it consumed my flesh and reached my bones and was roasted. Take it, crush it, and scatter it in the sea.’ They did that, and God Almighty gathered him to himself. Then He said to him: ‘Why did you do that?’ He said: ‘Out of fear of You.’ So God Almighty forgave him.” Uqbah ibn Amr said: I heard him, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that, and he was a grave robber. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair with many wordings, including that he ordered his sons to burn him, then crush him, then scatter half of him on land and half of him in the sea on a windy day, meaning a day with a lot of wind. They did that, and God Almighty ordered the sea, so it gathered what was in it, and He ordered the land, so it gathered what was in it, then He said to it: ‘Be.’ And behold, he was a man standing. He said to him: ‘What made you do what you did?’ He said: I feared you, and you know best. So he was forgiven for it. God the Almighty says: {Who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it} meaning He who began the creation of this tree from water until it became green and fresh, bearing fruit and ripening, then He returned it until it became dry wood with which fire is kindled. Thus, He is the Doer of whatever He wills, Able to do whatever He wants, nothing can prevent Him. Qatada said about His statement: {Who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it} meaning He who brought forth this fire from this tree is Able to resurrect it. It was also said that what is meant by this are the Marakh and Afar trees that grow in the land of Hijaz, so whoever wants to kindle a fire but does not have a flint, takes two green sticks and strikes one with the other, and fire is generated from between them, just like a flint. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him. In the proverb: Every tree has a fire, and Marakh and Afar are glorified. The wise men said: In every tree there is fire except the forest.

As Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Jarir told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Maysarah told me, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Bishr bin Jahash, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat one day into his hand, then placed his finger on it, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty said: Son of Adam, how can you outstrip Me when I created you from something like this, until, when I proportioned you and made you equal, you walked between your two garments, and the earth was slow from you. You gathered and withheld until, when you reached the collarbones, I said: ‘Shall I give charity?’ But when is the time for charity?” It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun on the authority of Jarir ibn Uthman on his authority. That is why God the Almighty said: “And he has presented to Us an example and forgotten his own creation. He says, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?’” That is, he doubted that God the Almighty, the One with the great power who created the heavens and the earth, would bring back the decayed bodies and bones. He forgot himself, and that God the Almighty created him from nothingness into existence. So he knew about himself something greater than what he doubted, denied, and rejected. That is why God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘He will give them life who produced them the first time. And He is Knowing of all creation.’” That is, He knows the bones in all parts of the earth and its regions, where they went and where they were scattered and torn apart. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Rab’i, who said: Uqba bin Amr said to Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with them both: Will you not tell us what you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: I heard him, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A man was dying, and when he despaired of life, he advised his family: ‘When I die, gather for me a large amount of firewood, then light a fire in it until it consumed my flesh and reached my bones and was roasted. Take it, crush it, and scatter it in the sea.’ They did that, and God Almighty gathered him to himself. Then He said to him: ‘Why did you do that?’ He said: ‘Out of fear of You.’ So God Almighty forgave him.” Uqbah ibn Amr said: I heard him, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that, and he was a grave robber. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair with many wordings, including that he ordered his sons to burn him, then crush him, then scatter half of him on land and half of him in the sea on a windy day, meaning a day with a lot of wind. They did that, and God Almighty ordered the sea, so it gathered what was in it, and He ordered the land, so it gathered what was in it, then He said to it: ‘Be.’ And behold, he was a man standing. He said to him: ‘What made you do what you did?’ He said: I feared you, and you know best. So he was forgiven for it. God the Almighty says: {Who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it} meaning He who began the creation of this tree from water until it became green and fresh, bearing fruit and ripening, then He returned it until it became dry wood with which fire is kindled. Thus, He is the Doer of whatever He wills, Able to do whatever He wants, nothing can prevent Him. Qatada said about His statement: {Who made for you fire from the green tree, and behold, you kindle from it} meaning He who brought forth this fire from this tree is Able to resurrect it. It was also said that what is meant by this are the Marakh and Afar trees that grow in the land of Hijaz, so whoever wants to kindle a fire but does not have a flint, takes two green sticks and strikes one with the other, and fire is generated from between them, just like a flint. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him. In the proverb: Every tree has a fire, and Marakh and Afar are glorified. The wise men said: In every tree there is fire except the forest.
36:81: God Almighty says, informing and drawing attention to His great power in creating the seven heavens and what they contain of planets and fixed stars, and the seven earths, and what they contain of mountains, sand, seas, deserts, and everything in between, and guiding us to the evidence for the restoration of bodies by the creation of these great things, as God Almighty says: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. And God Almighty says here: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? That is, like mankind, so He restores them as He began them. Ibn Jarir said: This noble verse is like God Almighty’s saying: Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth and did not become weary in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, He is over all things competent. And God Almighty says here: “Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. * His command when He intends a thing is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is.” That is, He only commands a thing with one command that does not need repetition or confirmation. If God wants something, He just says to it, Be, and it is. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Numayr told us, Musa bin Al-Musayyab told us, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanam, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: O My servants, all of you are sinners except for those I have pardoned, so seek My forgiveness and I will forgive you. All of you are poor except for those I have enriched. I am indeed Generous, Majestic and All-Powerful. I do what I will. My giving is speech and My punishment is speech. If I desire something, I only say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.” God the Almighty says: So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion over all things, and to Him you will be returned. That is, glorification, sanctification, and innocence from evil for the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, and to Him all matters will be returned. To Him belongs creation and command, and to Him will the servants return on the Day of Resurrection. He will reward every worker for his deeds, and He is the Just, the Beneficent, the Generous. The meaning of His Almighty saying: So exalted is He in whose hand is the dominion over all things, is like His saying: Say, ‘In whose hand is the dominion over all things?’ and His saying: Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion. So dominion and dominion are one in meaning, like mercy and compassion, awe and awe, compulsion and compulsion. Some people claim that dominion is the world of bodies, and dominion is the world of spirits. The first is correct, and it is what the majority of commentators and others believe. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj bin Al-Nu’man told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Hudhayfah’s cousin, who was Ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I stood with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night, and he recited the seven long verses in seven rak’ahs. Whenever he, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his head from bowing, he would say: ‘God hears whoever praises Him.’ Then he would say: ‘Praise be to God, Possessor of the Kingdom, Power, Pride, and Greatness.’ His bowing was like his standing, and his prostration was like his bowing. Then he left and my legs were almost broken.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi in Al-Shama’il, and Al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Shu’bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Hamzah, the freed slave of the Ansar, from a man from Banu Abs, from Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, “He saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying at night. He used to say: ‘God is Great’ three times, ‘Possessor of the Kingdom, Power, Pride, and Greatness.’ Then he began and recited Surat Al-Baqarah, then he bowed, and his bowing was approximately the same as his standing. He used to say in his bowing: ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty.’ Then he raised his head from bowing, and his standing was approximately the same as his bowing. He used to say in his standing: ‘Praise be to my Lord.’ Then he prostrated, and his prostration was approximately the same as his standing. He used to say in his al-Sajdah 32:‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’ Then he raised his head from prostration. He used to sit between the two prostrations for approximately the same length of his prostration. He used to say: ‘Lord, forgive me, Lord, forgive me.’ So he prayed four rak’ahs, and in them he recited Surat Al-Baqarah, Surat Al-Imran, Surat An-Nisa’, Surat Al-Ma’idah, or Surat Al-An’am.” Shu’bah was unsure. This is the wording of Abu Dawud. Dawud and An-Nasa'i said: Abu Hamza in our view is Talha ibn Yazid, and this man is likely to be Silah, as he said, and it is more likely that he is Hudhayfah's cousin, as mentioned previously in the narration of Imam Ahmad, and God knows best. As for the narration of Silah ibn Zafar on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, it is in Sahih Muslim, but it does not mention the kingdom, power, pride and greatness. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Salih told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, on the authority of Asim ibn Humayd, on the authority of Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I stood with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night, and he stood and recited Surat al-Baqarah. He did not pass by a verse of mercy without stopping and asking, and he did not pass by a verse of punishment without stopping and seeking refuge. Then he bowed for as long as he had stood, saying in his bowing: ‘Glory be to the Possessor of Majesty, Sovereignty, Pride, and Greatness.’ Then he prostrated for as long as he had stood, then he said the same in his prostration. Then he stood and recited Al Imran, then he recited Surat al-Sura.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Shama’il and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Muawiyah ibn Salih with it.
